question: Should Telegram message-cache persistence adopt a seven-day TTL, and if so should existing NULL-expiry rows be migrated through a Telegram/doctor path or by changing the generic plugin-state SDK contract?
rationale: Automation can identify the compatibility bug, but it cannot choose the durable retention policy or silently broaden the plugin-state contract for all plugin namespaces.

options.title: Scope And Rebase Before Merge
options.body: Keep the Telegram TTL only if maintainers accept it, refresh onto current main, and move NULL-row cleanup out of generic register/registerIfAbsent writes into a scoped Telegram migration or approved SDK path.

options.title: Adopt Generic TTL Migration Contract
options.body: If retroactive expiry for TTL-enabled namespaces is desired, update SDK docs and compatibility tests so plugin authors see the new contract before it ships.

options.title: Pause The Retention Follow-Up
options.body: Because the cap lockout was fixed separately, maintainers can defer or close this retention follow-up until Telegram reply-context lifetime is settled.

recommendation.title: Scope And Rebase Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the Telegram TTL only if maintainers accept it, refresh onto current main, and move NULL-row cleanup out of generic register/registerIfAbsent writes into a scoped Telegram migration or approved SDK path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared SQLite state and Telegram persistence work makes this the strongest routing candidate for the retention and migration-contract decision.
